how_it_was_made.method: Each model forecast each of the last 12 complete months using only the data that existed at the time, once from 1 month ahead and once from 2 months ahead. Among the models that can run (6+ scored months, and the budget model only when a budget is given), the one with the lowest average miss at each horizon makes the call.

what_would_make_it_wrong.evidence: Last year, like-for-like leads per day moved -23% from September 2025 to October 2025 and -24% to November 2025. Model C carries that turn into this year; model A would have said 289 leads for October at September's pace. If this autumn breaks from last year's shape (an early cold snap, a late heat spell), model C misses in that direction.

Calls from ads started counting in 2025-03 (26% of leads in its first 3 months). Model C reads the year before it like-for-like, so the extra counting doesn't look like growth. Adding or removing another conversion action would need the same treatment.
No step change found in cost per lead.
Spend is assumed to hold at the September 2026 pace ($12,102 in 30 days). Last year spend moved -5% from September 2025 to October 2025. A planned budget lets model D and the budget what-if run.

unknowns: No planned budget, so model D did not run and spend is assumed to hold at the September pace.
No real conversion value, so revenue is not forecast.
Only Google Ads is connected for this run, so the forecast covers paid search leads only.

what_would_make_it_wrong: Summer weather. July carries an index of 1.51 on Google Ads; a mild or a record summer moves the year more than any other month. Jul 2027 has the widest range: 471 to 909 leads.
Calls from ads are 17% of the plan-year leads and have only 19 months of history, so their share is the least tested part.
The launch estimate (+10% in Mar to Jun) is yours: it adds 160 leads. Without it, those months fall that much further from target.
Spend held at today's level: the gap needs at least $28,608 more in 2027 at forecast cost per lead, and cost per lead usually rises as spend rises, so treat it as a floor.
Months 7 to 12 ahead on Google Ads: 21 of 21 backtest months landed inside the ±32% band.
unknowns: Revenue rests on your close rate and average job; a 5-point change in close rate moves revenue by about 17%.
Search Console, GA4 and the store or CRM were not part of this run, so organic and offline leads are not in the totals.
Platform-claimed leads can overlap: one customer who clicks a Google ad and a Meta ad can count twice.
